sources.title: Shore Power Demand for South African Ports
method: TNPA vessel movement logs for financial years 2018–2025
Arrival/departure and berth-time reconstruction where needed
Vessel type normalization and vessel size proxies
Regression-based estimation of missing critical demand inputs
Estimated average-maximum and absolute-maximum shore-power demand time series
limitations: Some port/year data were omitted where vessel-type classification was incorrect.
Demand values are estimates derived from vessel activity and reference demand data, not port-side interval-meter measurements.
The estimate depends on vessel categorization, vessel size proxies, berth-time data and model assumptions.

sources.title: Load Connection Capacity Assessment of South African National Ports
method: Pre-feasibility review of port power-intake firm supply and notified maximum demand
Estimated spare MW calculated as 0.9 × (firm supply MVA − notified maximum demand MVA)
Connection-risk label based on estimated spare capacity
limitations: Risk labels are based solely on estimated spare capacity.
Ranking does not account for substation space, accessibility, electrical servitudes, routing or detailed connection requirements.
Upstream network capacity and utility/municipality connection studies remain necessary.
Estimated spare capacity at a port intake is not an allocation, connection offer or guarantee of firm capacity.

spare_capacity_estimation.note: The formula reproduces the report's estimated MW conversion; it is not a load-flow calculation or supply-authority approval.

suggested_reference_case_roles.rationale: Largest estimated shore-power average-maximum and absolute-maximum demands in the eight-port dataset.
Highest estimated spare port-intake capacity in the connection assessment, alongside a lower shore-power estimate than Durban or Cape Town.
Second-highest estimated shore-power demand with zero estimated spare port-intake capacity in the pre-feasibility ranking.
Useful industrial-port comparison, but this dataset contains no complete port-wide industrial demand profile.

prohibited_inferences: Do not treat shore_power_demand_estimates as directly metered port electrical loads.
Do not subtract spare port-intake capacity from shore-power demand as if both were a synchronized power-flow study.
Do not treat estimated spare capacity as a grid connection offer, reserved capacity or guaranteed firm supply.
Do not treat a connection-risk label as a complete grid feasibility result.
Do not infer site suitability, nuclear feasibility, nuclear safety, port authorization or community acceptance.
Do not size a reactor from shore-power demand alone.
Do not treat one annual peak or maximum as an hourly load curve.
required_next_evidence: Current port-side interval-meter data and synchronized berth/vessel schedules.
Current port single-line diagrams, substation and transformer ratings, protection studies and connection-point definition.
Utility/municipality/Eskom load-flow and N-1 connection study for each candidate configuration.
Port-wide industrial, city, cold-chain, water, shore-power and future expansion load profiles.
Tariff, demand-charge, curtailment, power-quality and connection-cost data with currency/base year.
